plain_english: So dharma and adharma, heaven and hell, birth and death, pleasure and pain — caste, life-stage and the rest — though unreal in the self, arise by delusion's force.
sanskrit_cite: tadvad dharmādharmasvarnirayotpattimaraṇasukhaduḥkham | varṇāśramādi cātmany asad api vibhramabalād bhavati

plain_english: This is that darkness: shining in things, the conceit 'I am not the self' arises even where the self is unsurpassed.
sanskrit_cite: etat tad andhakāraṃ yad bhāveṣu prakāśamānatayā | ātmānatirikteṣv api bhavaty anātmābhimāno 'yam

plain_english: Darkness upon darkness — a great burst upon the cheek: taking body, breath and the rest, non-selves, for self.
sanskrit_cite: timirād api timiram idaṃ ga.ṅdasyopari mahān ayaṃ sphoṭaḥ | yad anātmany api dehaprāṇadāv ātmamānitvam

plain_english: By the yoga of body, breath, reflection, mind, knowing, and sky-expanse, the self wraps itself — a wonder — in a net, like the net-maker.
sanskrit_cite: dehaprāṇavimarśanadhījñānanabhaḥprapañcayogena | ātmānam veṣṭayate citraṃ jālena jālakāra iva

plain_english: By the yoga that shines with one's own knowing glory, unwrapping one's own self: thus supreme Śiva spreads the wondrous play of bondage and release.
sanskrit_cite: svajñānavibhavabhāsanayogenodveṣṭayen nijātmānam | iti bandhamokṣacitrāṃ krīḍāṃ pratanoti paramaśivaḥ

plain_english: Creating, keeping, dissolving; waking, dreaming, deep sleep — they shine in him, in the fourth abode, yet unveiled he shines.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā jāgratsvapnau suṣuptam iti tasmin | bhānti turīye dhāmani tathāpi tair nāvṛtaṃ bhāti

plain_english: Waking is the universe, through difference; dreaming is splendor, through light's glory; the knower is the sleep state, through massed knowing; beyond that, the fourth.
sanskrit_cite: jāgrad viśvaṃ bhedāt svapnas tejaḥ prakāśamāhātmyāt | prājñaḥ suptāvasthā jñānaghanatvāt tataḥ paraṃ turyam

plain_english: As cloud, smoke and dust do not soil the sky's surface, so the supreme person stands untouched by Māyā's deformings.
sanskrit_cite: jaladharadhūmarajobhir malinīkriyate yathā na gaganatalam | tadvan māyāvikṛtibhir aparāmṛṣṭaḥ paraḥ puruṣaḥ

plain_english: When one jar-sky is pervaded by dust, the others do not get soiled: so these souls, enjoying pleasure-pain differences.
sanskrit_cite: ekasmin ghaṭagagane rajasā vyāpte bhavanti nānyāni | malināni tadvad ete jīvāḥ sukhaduḥkhabhedajuṣaḥ
